forbidden_clipping_patterns: Never spawn two characters at the same (x, y) coordinate
Never path a walkTo trajectory straight through a stationary actor's bounding box
Keep background crowd NPCs at least 4.5 studs behind foreground speakers (y >= 4.5)

custom_roblox_asset_builder_rules.instruction: Whenever the script mentions an object, prop, crown, vehicle, gadget, trophy, or structure not already present in standard places, Gemini MUST define it in `things` using blocky Roblox primitive parts (box/cylinder/sphere with exact size [w,d,h], pos [x,y,z], and bright hex color) and target it with `cam: 'ins', focus: '<ThingName>'` during key reveal beats.

sample_hook_formulas: The 'Underdog Secret' hook: Starts with a high-stakes social vulnerability ('no super power') combined with a relatable romantic motivation ('impress my crush') within the first 1.5 seconds to trigger immediate empathy and curiosity.
The 'In this town, nothing grew' opening establishes a high-stakes mystery and a 'curse' narrative, creating immediate curiosity about why the protagonist defies the impossible.
High-concept binary world setup with a striking split-color visual aesthetic ('In this world, everything is either blue or pink') combined with rapid movement and immediate high-stakes worldbuilding.

The hook uses a high-stakes narrative premise ('Whoever reaches the top... gets to marry the girl') combined with a visual 'failure montage' that creates immediate curiosity about the protagonist's eventual success.
High-stakes dystopian hook. Protagonist wastes his last 7 lifetime words on a question, setting his counter to zero as a creepy robot speaks in his dad's voice.
High-stakes supernatural exile premise paired with fast action immediately pulls viewers into the narrative.

Establishes a high-stakes secret dynamic immediately ('My crush's twin brother has been my best friend for a year') using a close two-shot and snappy subtitle pacing to trigger instant curiosity about identity and deception.

High-concept world-building rule delivered instantly in the first 1.5 seconds ('At my school, whatever your t-shirt says, you are'), pairing a striking visual (Roblox character wearing a crown and plain blue shirt) with immediate intrigue about societal rules.

In this world, you can only eat foods that start with the first letter of your name. (Establishes an absurd, high-stakes absolute rule in under 3 seconds using direct visual demonstration of eggs, preventing scroll-away by introducing instant surrealism).
High-stakes mystery countdown paired with epic army conflict forces immediate curiosity about the white tower's secret.
Absurd romantic premise ('brought her the moon') immediately driving action and curiosity.
Presents a high-stakes supernatural constraint ('We only move when the eye blinks') combined with an extreme close-up of a giant floating eye to instantly trigger curiosity.
Absurdist paradox hook pairing high-stakes tragedy with instant comedic denial to prevent scrolling.
Instant absurd transformation hook (witch curses crush into a 90yo grandma with a walker at school), pairing immediate visual contradiction with high-stakes teenage romance.

Subverted childhood game nostalgia ('Heads Up, Seven Up') turned into high-stakes psychological horror within 0-3 seconds; immediate visual shock of an ink-black tally-covered giant looming over obediently bowed children.

High-stakes supernatural rule hook: Stating an absurd, impossible condition ('Every boy who asks my crush out gets struck by lightning') paired with immediate visual proof (boy holding flowers getting zapped) and escalating personal consequence ('I've been struck 11 times').
Immediate 0-3s high-stakes action line with crash-in zoom and rapid visual cut

High-concept absurd premise delivered instantly ('Every time I talked to my crush, something falls from the sky') paired with an immediate visual gag (a piano crashing down), stopping the scroll by creating instant narrative curiosity and dark comedy.

The hook uses a 'forbidden action' trope: 'if you make a grown-up turn the car around, you never come home.' It creates immediate high stakes by linking a common childhood experience (kicking a seat) to a supernatural, irreversible consequence.
Relatable high-stakes social anxiety: Kiss cam highlights MC and crush in a packed stadium.
High-stakes romantic premise with extreme numbers (900 geniuses) to capture instant interest.
High-stakes romantic tension + isolation hook ('stuck in a hot spring with my crush'). Stops scrolling using instant teenage relatable vulnerability.
Surreal existential threat paired with an extreme macro visual of a giant human thumb resting on book text.
Forbidden rule premise setup creates instant conflict and high-stakes social tension.
High-concept sensory connection premise paired with immediate dramatic action to stop scrolling.
sample_story_arcs: Setup: Protagonist fakes powers at superhero school to hide his normalcy. Escalation: Weird phenomena occur (floating stops, fire dies) whenever he is near his crush. Twist/Payoff: A villain attack reveals his true power is a 'power nullifier,' which explains the previous anomalies and leads to a romantic resolution.

Setup: Theo's obsession with the barren hill. Escalation: Decades of ridicule and persistent planting. Twist/Payoff: The hill saves the town from a mudslide, revealing Rosa as the secret benefactor who supported him all along.

Setup: Introduction of the strictly segregated blue and pink world and the giant balance scale -> Escalation: Daily tank battles, Rose getting captured and turned pink, the protagonists stealing a blue tank to fight back -> Climax/Twist: Leo getting hit by both blue and pink balloons simultaneously, creating a new purple world -> Payoff/CTA: Call to action for viewers to comment 'Leo' to save the purple world.

Setup: The impossible tower challenge and the girl inside. Escalation: A series of escalating, humorous failed attempts by various archetypes (knight, prince, wizard, protagonist). Twist/Payoff: The protagonist realizes the door was never locked, subverting the 'climbing' trope with a simple, grounded solution.

Setup: Protagonist exhausts his remaining words asking a robot about his dad. Escalation: Flees through a dystopian city where zero-word citizens are harvested by collector robots. Twist/Payoff: Dad's robot guides him to the master mic to trigger global shutdown—revealing all robots were actually converted humans now permanently disabled.

Setup: An exiled goddess moves in with the town's worst kid. Escalation: Misunderstandings and magic ruin his attempts at good deeds. Twist: The goddess deliberately sabotaged him to avoid returning to Heaven. Payoff: He intentionally breaks rules to stay with her.

Setup: Protagonist befriends the twin brother of his crush while struggling to talk to the girl at school. Escalation: Daily conversations about the crush reveal oddly specific inside knowledge, high voice, pulled-down cap, and dropped objects. Climax/Twist: Inviting both to a birthday party leads to the 'brother' disappearing and the crush walking out holding his cap, revealing the twin never existed and she disguised herself.

Setup (explaining the school shirt rules and eccentric classmates) -> Escalation (new principal Mr. Pickett enforces strict control via spirit shirts and hidden text) -> Climax/Twist (students lift Mr. Pickett, his blazer opens revealing 'PRINCIPAL', then protagonist orchestrates mass rebellion by turning shirts inside out at three o'clock, stripping the principal of his power and restoring true friendship).

Setup: Introduce the arbitrary town rule where names dictate diets and mayors must be named Pete. Escalation: Ezra highlights his miserable 3,000-day egg diet and lists three strange clues in the museum (rigged laws, unused balloon catcher, and baby Zachary Paul). Twist/Payoff: Ezra realizes it's a centuries-old political conspiracy, eats pizza in public, proves magic doesn't exist, and overthrows the mayor into a life of forced zucchini.

Two kingdoms wage endless war over a mysterious counting tower. As the countdown hits zero, a commander enters and discovers it is a space rocket holding civilized survivors who flee the warlike surface.
Setup: Protagonist seeks moon for crush -> Escalation: Failed DIY rocket launches -> Climax: Lunar landing in dad's car -> Twist: Rescued her missing cat 'Moon' eating his lunches.

Setup: A city lives under a floating eye, moving only during its blinks. Escalation: The eye stops blinking, freezing the population except the protagonist who turns around. Twist/Payoff: The eye wasn't watching them, but holding a colossal mountain monster at bay—and it's about to blink.
Premise setup (fake death) -> Escalation (absurdist funeral speeches) -> Payoff (crush confession and discovery).

Setup: Crush is cursed into an elderly woman struggling through normal school routines. Escalation: Hero discovers brave acts subtract one year of age and sets up stunts. Payoff: Stunts are too slow, so hero takes the ultimate brave risk by asking her out, breaking the curse instantly.

Setup: A lethal ritual occurs daily at 3:00 PM where a tally-marked monster presses one thumb to abduct a sixth-grader, while the narrator survives by interlocking pinkies with best friend Nico. Escalation: Class population steadily drops from 30 to 2 as desks pile higher than the school gym; clues surface through Nico's chalk-stained hands and a classmate noting the monster's touch felt warm like a child's finger. Climax & Twist: On the final day with only two kids left, Nico sacrifices himself with a chalk mark, revealing he was forced to choose the victims every day to save the protagonist. Payoff: Protagonist looks up, breaking the fatal rule, as the monster turns toward them while Nico gives one final bittersweet smile.

Setup (supernatural curse on crush striking suitors with lightning) -> Escalation montage (protagonist attempts asking her out with rubber suit, car, bucket, bleacher spectators, hospital visit) -> Detective revelation (discovering the cloud is sentient and in love with her) -> Creative resolution (wingman play: building a pink fog machine girlfriend for the cloud) -> Romantic success & comedic punchline (crush says yes, dad still misses his fog machine).
Fast hook -> rapid escalating micro-beats -> sudden twist -> comedic/dramatic payoff

Setup: Protagonist introduces the curse where objects fall from the sky when talking to his crush. Escalation: Objects get progressively bigger (flower pot, bathtub, piano, canoe, shopping cart) as he tries helmets and friends. Clue discovery: He notices a tiny bell and scratch marks. Twist/Payoff: He confesses anyway, looks up, and discovers her cat has been maliciously pushing objects off the roof all year; the cat drops a single rose instead of a car to seal the romance.

Setup: Establishing the urban legend of the 'wrong way' road. Escalation: The protagonist's brother triggers the curse, causing the mother to vanish. Twist/Payoff: The protagonist and Grandpa enter the void to rescue them, discovering that a second 'turn around' (kicking the seat again) acts as a reset button to return home.

Setup: Kiss cam targets MC and crush; MC awkwardly tries to dodge public pressure. Escalation: MC finds out crush paid the cameraman $20 to target them. Twist: MC pays $40 for a second attempt. Payoff: They lean in for the kiss but MC gets hit in the face by a soccer ball.

background_and_lighting_standards.background_prop_density: Moderate, clean low-poly composition where props (modular houses, low-poly faceted trees, sandbags, desks, target boards) are arranged along clear horizontal and vertical axes deep in Z-space, leaving 60% of the upper and central vertical frame unobstructed for bold typography and avatar silhouettes.
background_and_lighting_standards.lighting_contrast: High-key, vibrant directional daylight with sharp, minimal ambient occlusion shadows and vivid skies (saturated cyan, bubblegum pink, or golden sunset). Shadows never cast muddy pitch-black values onto skin tones; characters receive crisp rim-lighting to remain instantly readable against complex background scenery.

shot_sequence_signatures: WS (establishing world conflict) -> MCU (protagonist reaction) -> INS (absurd prop reveal) -> MCU (emotional realization) -> TWO (resolution)
TWO (side-by-side confrontation) -> CU (rival smug expression) -> CU (hero shock/sweat) -> FS (slapstick motion) -> MCU (punchline)
LOW (towering hazard/structure) -> FS (protagonist attempting obstacle) -> INS (failure/drop detail) -> MCU (distressed reaction)
OTS (crush or villain reveal) -> MCU (hero awkward eye contact) -> INS (crucial physical detail/rope cut) -> TWO (intimate shared bench shot)
FS (split-color boundary line) -> HIGH (armies lined up at sandbags) -> MCU (determined command) -> LOW (massive vehicle roll-in)
POV (under-bed framing) -> LOW (giant robot limbs pacing) -> CU (countdown badge decrement) -> MCU (hero scream/panic)
camera_and_staging_rules.prop_zoom_rules: Extreme close-up inserts (INS) framed at a 15-30 degree downward angle centered directly at the mid-screen crosshair. Key narrative props (library overdue stamps, ankle ropes, cardboard vehicle wheels, dropped pillows, leaf blowers) scale to occupy 40% to 65% of screen width with bold color separation against the surface behind them.
camera_and_staging_rules.character_spacing_and_poses: R6 blocky rigs are staged with a mandatory 1.2 to 1.6 stud horizontal gap during standing two-shots to prevent arm and shoulder mesh penetration. Seated characters snap their legs parallel to seat edges with torsos rotated 12-18 degrees inward toward their partner. Expressive poses use clear, exaggerated arm angles (35-45 degrees outward for running or panicked gestures, 90-degree right angles for pointing and holding props) ensuring clean readability without visual clipping.
